rows.section: Contractors: employee or contractor, and schedular payments
rows.label: Tax test: employee or contractor (Inland Revenue)
rows.value: Generally an employee if the payer controls how and when the work is done. Indicators: must do the work personally; told what to do, when and how; paid a set rate; can get overtime or penal rates; set hours; works at the payer's premises; the payer sets the standards
rows.note: Schedular tax is a prepayment of the contractor's income tax, squared up in the annual return.
rows.source_title: Inland Revenue: Employer's guide, IR335 (September 2026), pages 8 and 14-17

rows.section: Contractors: employee or contractor, and schedular payments
rows.label: Tax guidance: Interpretation Guideline IG 16/01
rows.value: Common-law tests: intention, control, independence, fundamental (in business on their own account) and integration; leading case Bryson v Three Foot Six Ltd [2005] NZSC 34
rows.note: Schedular tax is a prepayment of the contractor's income tax, squared up in the annual return.
rows.source_title: Inland Revenue (Tax technical): Interpretation Guideline IG 16/01, Determining employment status for tax purposes (employee or independent contractor?), issued 8 March 2016, paragraphs 5-6

rows.section: Contractors: employee or contractor, and schedular payments
rows.label: Employment law: gateway test (from 21 February 2026)
rows.value: A worker is a contractor if all criteria are met: a written agreement saying they are a contractor or not an employee; free to work for others; can choose when to work or subcontract; can decline extra work; had a chance to get independent advice. Otherwise the common-law test applies
rows.note: Schedular tax is a prepayment of the contractor's income tax, squared up in the annual return.
rows.source_title: Employment New Zealand (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment): Employee or contractor

rows.section: Contractors: employee or contractor, and schedular payments
rows.label: Schedular payments: form and tax code
rows.value: The contractor gives the payer a Tax rate notification for contractors (IR330C); the payer deducts withholding tax at the chosen or standard rate and reports it under tax code WT. Activities not listed on the IR330C have no deduction
rows.note: Schedular tax is a prepayment of the contractor's income tax, squared up in the annual return.
rows.source_title: Inland Revenue: Payroll Calculations & Business Rules Specification 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027 (24 March 2026, v1.0), sections 5.14, 5.14.1, 5.14.2; Employer's guide IR335 (September 2026), pages 13, 16-17

rows.label: Tax resident after more than this many days in New Zealand in any 12-month period

rows.section: Non-residents: tax residence and employment income
rows.label: Permanent place of abode
rows.value: A place in New Zealand where you usually live also makes you resident, whichever test is met first
rows.note: Recognised Seasonal Employer and fishing crew visa holders do not become resident after 183 days unless they have a permanent place of abode.
rows.source_title: Inland Revenue: Tax residency status for individuals (last updated 25 June 2026)

rows.section: Non-residents: tax residence and employment income

rows.source_title: Inland Revenue: Tax residency status for individuals (last updated 25 June 2026)

rows.section: Non-residents: tax residence and employment income
rows.label: Non-resident visitor: up to this many days in New Zealand in any 18-month period
rows.note: only if not working for or paid by a New Zealand resident or a New Zealand branch, among other conditions
rows.source_title: Inland Revenue: Tax residency status for individuals (last updated 25 June 2026)

rows.section: Non-residents: tax residence and employment income
rows.label: Non-residents: tax on New Zealand employment income
rows.value: Taxed on New Zealand-source income; the employer deducts PAYE in the same way as for any other employee (the income tax rates above), including the ACC earners' levy
rows.note: Recognised Seasonal Employer and fishing crew visa holders do not become resident after 183 days unless they have a permanent place of abode.
rows.source_title: Inland Revenue: Employer's guide, IR335 (September 2026), page 54 (Non-residents)

rows.label: Who sets rates
rows.value: City and district councils and regional councils, under the Local Government (Rating) Act 2002
rows.note: Rates differ by council and are not stored here; the 2026/27 rates rebate amounts are not stored because the official order could not be read.
rows.source_title: Local Government (Rating) Act 2002

rows.label: Base
rows.value: Property value: each council chooses land value, capital value or annual value and sets a cents-in-the-dollar rate each year
rows.note: Rates differ by council and are not stored here; the 2026/27 rates rebate amounts are not stored because the official order could not be read.
rows.source_title: Local Government (Rating) Act 2002

rows.label: Targeted and differential rates
rows.value: Targeted rates fund particular services (on value, land area, floor space, connections and other factors); general rates may differ by location, use or area
rows.note: Rates differ by council and are not stored here; the 2026/27 rates rebate amounts are not stored because the official order could not be read.
rows.source_title: Local Government (Rating) Act 2002

rows.label: Uniform annual general charge
rows.value: A fixed charge per rating unit, whatever the property value
rows.note: Rates differ by council and are not stored here; the 2026/27 rates rebate amounts are not stored because the official order could not be read.
rows.source_title: Local Government (Rating) Act 2002

rows.label: Cap on fixed charges (uniform annual general charge plus fixed targeted rates), share of total rates revenue
rows.note: Rates differ by council and are not stored here; the 2026/27 rates rebate amounts are not stored because the official order could not be read.
rows.source_title: Local Government (Rating) Act 2002

rows.label: Reliefs
rows.value: Remissions and postponements under each council's policy; the Rates Rebate Scheme for low-income homeowners (apply to the council)
rows.note: Rates differ by council and are not stored here; the 2026/27 rates rebate amounts are not stored because the official order could not be read.
rows.source_title: Local Government (Rating) Act 2002

rows.label: Rates of each council
rows.value: Set and published by each council; council profiles at localcouncils.govt.nz
rows.note: Rates differ by council and are not stored here; the 2026/27 rates rebate amounts are not stored because the official order could not be read.
rows.source_title: Local Government (Rating) Act 2002

rows.label: Stamp duty or property transfer tax
rows.value: None: conveyance duty on residential property was repealed in 1988, and the Stamp Duty Abolition Act 1999 abolished the remaining conveyance and lease duty for instruments executed after 20 May 1999
rows.source_title: Inland Revenue: Tax Information Bulletin Vol 11 No 5 (May/June 1999), page 4: Stamp Duty Abolished (Stamp Duty Abolition Act 1999)

rows.label: Overseas buyers (consent rules, not a tax)
rows.value: Overseas people usually cannot buy a house or land; residence-class visa holders who are not yet ordinarily resident need consent; Australian and Singaporean citizens can buy residential property
rows.source_title: Toitū Te Whenua Land Information New Zealand: Buying residential property to live in (last updated 6 March 2026)

rows.label: Bright-line test (income tax on the seller)
rows.value: Profit on residential property sold within 2 years is taxable, unless an exclusion applies (sales on or after 1 July 2024)
rows.source_title: Inland Revenue: Tax for non-resident taxpayers (last updated 1 April 2026), Buying and selling New Zealand property

rows.section: Tax inventory: companies, contractors, non-residents and property
rows.label: Company tax (income tax on companies) [national]
rows.value: 28% for most companies, 17.5% for Māori authorities; GloBE multinational top-up tax up to a 15% effective rate for groups with revenue over EUR 750 million (IIR and UTPR from 2025, DIIR from 2026). Paid by companies. Income Tax Act 2007; GloBE rules added by the Taxation (Annual Rates for 2023-24, Multinational Tax, and Remedial Matters) Act 2024
rows.note: This list covers company tax, contractors, the self-employed, non-residents and property. Each row has its own source.
rows.source_title: Inland Revenue: Tax rates for businesses (last updated 1 April 2024)

rows.section: Tax inventory: companies, contractors, non-residents and property
rows.label: Branch profits tax or tax on distributed profits
rows.value: No separate tax: Inland Revenue lists none. A non-resident company with a permanent establishment in New Zealand is taxed on income derived here (company rate 28%); dividends carry imputation credits
rows.note: This list covers company tax, contractors, the self-employed, non-residents and property. Each row has its own source.
rows.source_title: Inland Revenue: Tax residency status for companies (last updated 25 June 2025)

rows.section: Tax inventory: companies, contractors, non-residents and property
rows.label: Self-employed contributions: ACC levies [national]
rows.value: Earners' levy 1.75% including GST on liable earnings of $50,501 to $156,641 (2026/27); Work levy by ACC classification unit (average 0.69%). Paid by self-employed people, invoiced by ACC. Accident Compensation Act 2001
rows.note: This list covers company tax, contractors, the self-employed, non-residents and property. Each row has its own source.
rows.source_title: Inland Revenue: Payroll Calculations & Business Rules Specification 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027 (24 March 2026, v1.0), section 2.1; Employer's guide IR335 (September 2026), page 16

rows.section: Tax inventory: companies, contractors, non-residents and property
rows.label: Contractor rules: schedular payments (withholding tax) [national]
rows.value: Standard rates 10.5% to 33% by activity, chosen rates from 10% (15% for non-residents), 45% without a notification; non-resident contractors 15%. Paid by contractors, deducted by the payer as a prepayment of income tax. Income Tax Act 2007 (schedular payments) and Tax Administration Act 1994
rows.note: This list covers company tax, contractors, the self-employed, non-residents and property. Each row has its own source.
rows.source_title: Inland Revenue: Payroll Calculations & Business Rules Specification 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027 (24 March 2026, v1.0), sections 5.14, 5.14.1, 5.14.2; Employer's guide IR335 (September 2026), pages 13, 16-17

rows.section: Tax inventory: companies, contractors, non-residents and property
rows.label: Simplified or presumptive regime for the self-employed
rows.value: None: self-employed people pay income tax on net profit at the individual rates through an individual return; GST registration is required above $60,000 a year
rows.note: This list covers company tax, contractors, the self-employed, non-residents and property. Each row has its own source.
rows.source_title: Inland Revenue: Self-employed (last updated 6 July 2026)

rows.section: Tax inventory: companies, contractors, non-residents and property
rows.label: Non-resident tax on employment income (PAYE) [national]
rows.value: The income tax rates (10.5% to 39%) through PAYE plus the ACC earners' levy, without the IETC; 10.5% flat for recognised seasonal workers (NSW). Paid by non-resident employees, deducted by the employer. Income Tax Act 2007; double tax agreements may exempt
rows.note: This list covers company tax, contractors, the self-employed, non-residents and property. Each row has its own source.
rows.source_title: Inland Revenue: Employer's guide, IR335 (September 2026), page 54 (Non-residents)

rows.section: Tax inventory: companies, contractors, non-residents and property
rows.label: Local council rates (property tax) [local]
rows.value: Set by each council each year on land, capital or annual value; fixed charges at most 30% of rates revenue. Paid by owners of rateable land. Local Government (Rating) Act 2002
rows.note: This list covers company tax, contractors, the self-employed, non-residents and property. Each row has its own source.
rows.source_title: Local Government (Rating) Act 2002

rows.section: Tax inventory: companies, contractors, non-residents and property
rows.label: Property transfer tax or stamp duty
rows.value: None: stamp duty was abolished (residential conveyance duty in 1988, all remaining conveyance and lease duty for instruments executed after 20 May 1999)
rows.note: This list covers company tax, contractors, the self-employed, non-residents and property. Each row has its own source.
